references.source:
Seung Kim, Sayed Ahmad, Amy Kim, and Mridul Sangma\.
The koch of bangladesh: a sociolinguistic survey\.
SIL Electronic Survey Report 2011\-023, SIL International, March 2011\.
One printed line lists a form together with every site that gave it, so a line stands for as many attestations as it carries site codes\. Lexical\-similarity groups are preserved as notes but are not treated as etymological or cognacy claims\. No unresolved modifier is inferred; 225 ambiguity\-only conceptual cells plus the unresolved variant at mixed item 241/site r remain auditable but uninstalled\.
URL: [https://www\.silbangladesh\.org/resources/archives/41580](https://www.silbangladesh.org/resources/archives/41580)\.
references.progress: Appendix A.3, "Wordlists": resolved attestations for items 1--307 at the four Koch target sites b, c, q and r (Nokshi, Kholchanda and Chandabhoi for Tintekiya Koch; Uttor Nokshi for Chapra Koch). The A'tong comparison sites l and m, standard Bangla comparison site 0, printed no-entry and not-used rows, and every modifier-bearing ambiguous row remain audit-only
references.provenance: Freely published SIL Electronic Survey Report; the publisher PDF is not redistributed. Canonical 91-page PDF SHA-256 d1b2d597c16fd0338ad47d2bf031566192c5ff4e26a6651de14a228df681fc10. Every lexical cell was independently transcribed and visually rechecked from rendered physical pages 43--62; frozen manual ledgers, source manifest, post-freeze reconciliation, staging audit and staged forms are under data/other/forms/raw_data/sil_kochbd_2011_manual/; installed rows are in data/other/forms/20260826-sil-kochbd.csv
references.locator: p. 54, wordlist item 198, site q Uttor Nokshi

references.source:

Bishnupriya \(manipuri\) speakers in bangladesh: a sociolinguistic survey\.

Site codes are a Tilakpur, b Soi Sri, c Gulerhaor, d Dhonitila, e Machimpur, f Madhapur and 0 standard Bangla\. Gulerhaor, Dhonitila, Soi Sri and Machimpur are Rajar Gang villages; Tilakpur and Madhapur are Madoi Gang villages\. One item 267 control code is visibly printed as lowercase o and is interpreted as 0 in the audit\.
URL: [https://www\.sil\.org/resources/archives/9100](https://www.sil.org/resources/archives/9100)\.
references.progress: Appendix B.3, "Wordlists": every printed response for the 307-item list, expanded across the six Bishnupriya village codes. The standard Bangla code 0, nine prompt headings with no responses, lexical-similarity calculations and all non-lexical appendices are audit-only
references.provenance: Freely published SIL Electronic Survey Report. The official SIL archive record and browser-rendered PDF are the bibliographic authority. Because the command-line publisher endpoint returned a Cloudflare HTML challenge, extraction used the fixed-layout text transcript and 2048-pixel page rasters in public Slideshare copy 2624796 as a mechanical scaffold. Reproducible extraction and the complete page and glyph fingerprints are in data/other/forms/raw_data/sil_bishnupriya_2008; per-record audit data are in data/other/forms/raw_data/20260828-sil-bishnupriya-audit.csv; installed rows are in data/other/forms/20260828-sil-bishnupriya.csv
references.locator: Appendix B.3, printed p. 46, item 198, Dhonitila; Appendix B.3, printed p. 46, item 198, Machimpur

references.source:
Amy Kim, Seung Kim, Palash Roy Sangma, and Mridul Ahmad\.
The tripura of bangladesh: a sociolinguistic survey\.
SIL Electronic Survey Report 2011\-038, SIL International, 2011\.
One printed line lists a form together with every site that gave it, so a line stands for as many attestations as it carries site codes\. Parenthesised material marks affixes, which the report treated as optional when comparing; it is preserved here\. Verbs \(items 171–222\) were elicited in the present continuous for Kok Borok, as commands for Garo and as verbal nouns for Bangla\.

references.progress: Appendix A.3, "Wordlists": every elicitation printed for the 306-item list across all twenty-four survey sites -- twenty Kok Borok villages, the three Garo wordlists (Abeng, Chibok and A'tong) and the standard Bangla list. Excludes the printed gaps marked "no entry", the lexical-similarity counting procedures (A.1), the wordlist notes (A.2) and the report's non-lexical appendices

The survey combines wordlists elicited during 1998 fieldwork with lists reused from earlier Bhil\-country, Dhule, Garasia, Dungra Bhil and Ahirani studies\. Source lexical\-similarity category numbers are retained only in Notes and do not assert historical cognacy\.
